notes.meaning: God describes how He used Babylon as His hammer to crush all kinds of people without mercy. Young and old, male and female, no one was spared when Babylon's armies swept through. Even though God used them to discipline nations, Babylon showed brutal cruelty to everyone in its path.

The list of destruction continues through every walk of life, from poor field workers to powerful rulers. Shepherds, farmers, and high officials were all crushed alike by Babylon's conquests. No group or rank of people could resist Babylon when God used it as His instrument of war.

God turns from using Babylon to judging it, promising to pay the empire back for its sins. The Jewish people would see Babylon punished for the terrible destruction it brought upon Jerusalem and the temple. God holds even the tools He uses accountable for their own wickedness.

The Lord declares war on Babylon, calling it a destroying mountain because of its towering pride and huge walls, even though it sat on a flat plain. Like a fiery volcano that once wrecked everything around it, Babylon will be toppled from its heights and burned out completely. No human empire can stand when God sets His hand against it.

Babylon will be so thoroughly ruined that nothing useful will be salvaged from its remains, not even stones to start a new building. Its collapse will be permanent, leaving no future empire or royal line to rise from its rubble.

differ.view: Some evangelicals believe Babylon must be rebuilt and destroyed in the end times, because the ancient city was not completely flattened when Cyrus captured it.

notes.meaning: God calls the surrounding nations to gather their armies for battle against Babylon, signaling them with war banners and trumpets. Kingdoms from the northern mountains of Armenia and Asia Minor are summoned to join the fight under Cyrus. Their cavalry will pour in like an unstoppable cloud of locusts.

God commands the rulers of Media and all their allied leaders to prepare themselves for battle. Media, joined with Persia, led the vast coalition that would bring down the Babylonian empire. God directs earthly leaders to carry out His righteous plans.

The land trembles in fear under the march of invading armies and the weight of God's coming judgment. Earthly powers may shake, but the Lord's settled purpose to leave Babylon completely empty and ruined will never fail.

Babylon's famous soldiers lose all courage and refuse to fight, hiding inside their fortresses instead. Their strength vanishes in panic, and the enemy breaks through the city gates and sets houses on fire. Human might fails completely when God removes a nation's courage.

Runners sprint from every direction toward the palace, bringing urgent news that the city has been breached. Because Babylon was so massive, outer parts of the city fell while the royal court was still feasting, completely unaware of the danger.

The river crossings and boat ferries around the Euphrates are captured, cutting off any chance of escape. The invaders set fire to the thick reed beds along the riverbanks, stripping away the soldiers' hiding places and leaving them paralyzed with fear.

God compares Babylon to a flat threshing floor being packed down hard in preparation for harvest work. Just as farmers trample the ground and then crush the wheat to separate the grain, God is preparing Babylon to be crushed in judgment. The time for Babylon to pay for its sins is rapidly approaching.

Jerusalem cries out to God, describing how King Nebuchadnezzar swallowed up the nation like a greedy sea monster. He looted all of Judah's treasures, broke the people's strength, and cast away the empty shell of their land. God hears His people's honest cries when they have been deeply wronged.

The people of Jerusalem pray that the cruelty and bloodshed they suffered will fall back on the Babylonians who caused it. This is a plea for divine justice, asking God to hold the violent conquerors guilty of murder.

The Lord answers Zion's cry by promising to serve as her legal defender and avenge her suffering. He will dry up Babylon's water defenses, which literally occurred when Cyrus diverted the Euphrates River to enter the city. God faithfully defends those who cannot defend themselves.

The once-glorious capital will be reduced to piles of broken bricks where only wild animals live. Travelers who pass by will gasp in shock and hiss with contempt at how far the mighty city has fallen.

The Babylonians shout and boast loudly, sounding like hungry young lions eager for food. This captures the reckless, confident noise of the Babylonians as they partied, unaware that disaster was right at the door.

While the Babylonian nobles are heated with wine and partying merrily, God prepares a deadly cup of judgment for them. This was fulfilled when Cyrus captured the city during Belshazzar's drunken feast, and the rulers were killed in their drunken stupor, sleeping the sleep of death.

The Babylonians who once acted like fierce lions are now led away as helpless as sheep and goats to the butcher. Both rulers and ordinary citizens will be swept away together without any ability to resist God's judgment.

The prophet expresses amazement that Sheshach, a coded name for Babylon, has fallen so suddenly. The city admired across the world for its size and splendor has become a terrifying picture of ruin. No worldly fame or glory can protect against the judgment of God.
An overwhelming sea of enemy soldiers washes over Babylon like crashing storm waves. The image shows how the Medes and Persians swept into the city in numbers too great to hold back.

The surrounding towns and countryside of Babylonia will turn into an empty, waterless wasteland. The irrigation canals will fail, leaving the ground so barren that no one will live there or even travel through it.
